verdict.label: Instant
verdict.oneLiner: Self-serve and no review: register an OAuth App and any GitHub user can authorize it.

steps.title: Choose OAuth App or GitHub App
steps.detail: GitHub recommends GitHub Apps for new work. Pick an OAuth App only if you need user-level access with a simple flow.
steps.agentAction: Compare permission models against your feature list.

steps.title: Register the OAuth App
steps.detail: Open Developer settings, choose New OAuth App, fill name, homepage URL and callback URL.

steps.title: Set one callback URL
steps.detail: Register the exact callback you will use. Sources disagree on multiple callbacks (see the uncertainties), so plan for one.
steps.agentAction: Derive the callback URL from your deployment host.

steps.title: Create a client secret
steps.detail: Generate a secret on the app page and store it in your server environment. Never commit it.

steps.title: Run the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Authorize with your own account and exchange the code for a token.

steps.title: Share the authorize link with other users
steps.detail: No review stands between you and other users.

blockers.cause: The redirect_uri in the request does not match the callback registered on the app.
blockers.fix: Register the exact URL (scheme, host, port, path) or send the registered one.
